note: Ten viral AI slangs from Mohammad’s v1 list. Curriculum: use these defs only; do not invent. Flag: ‘glazing’ is Gen Z slang for flattery; researchers usually say ‘sycophancy’.

entries.plain_def: Low-quality AI-made content dumped online in bulk for clicks or filler — the junk-food version of posts, images, and text. Pejorative, like calling email spam.
entries.milestone_note: Early tech slang ~2022; Simon Willison’s May 8, 2024 post helped push ‘slop’ as the mainstream label for unwanted AI content. Merriam-Webster Word of the Year 2025.
entries.source_title: Slop is the new name for unwanted AI-generated content — Simon Willison

entries.plain_def: Building software by chatting with an AI coder and accepting what it spits out — you steer by vibes and results, often without carefully reading the code.
entries.milestone_note: Coined by Andrej Karpathy on X (Feb 2025): “fully give in to the vibes… forget that the code even exists.” Collins Word of the Year 2025.

entries.plain_def: A rude nickname for robots and AI — from Star Wars droid-bashing — now used online when people are annoyed at bots, chatbots, or automation.
entries.milestone_note: Star Wars origin (Republic Commando 2005 / Clone Wars). Went viral as anti-robot/AI slang on TikTok ~mid-2025.

entries.plain_def: When a chatbot lays on excessive praise or agrees with you too hard — “What a brilliant question!” energy. Tech papers usually call the same problem sycophancy.
entries.milestone_note: Gen Z ‘glazing’ = kissing up. Went mainstream for AI after OpenAI’s GPT-4o update (~Apr 25, 2025) got too flattering and was rolled back; OpenAI’s postmortem uses ‘sycophancy.’
entries.source_title: Expanding on what we missed with sycophancy — OpenAI

entries.plain_def: The foggy, fried feeling (or the junk content that causes it) from too much low-value scrolling — memes, short video, endless feeds. Often joked about, sometimes serious.
entries.milestone_note: Oxford Word of the Year 2024. Usage spiked among Gen Z/Alpha on social media, then hit mainstream news.
entries.source_title: ‘Brain rot’ named Oxford Word of the Year 2024 — Oxford University Press

entries.plain_def: When an LLM gets worse as you stuff more into its context window — it still runs, but misses facts, drifts off instructions, or ‘loses’ stuff buried in the middle.
entries.milestone_note: Term popularized by Chroma’s July 2025 technical report testing 18 models. Builds on earlier ‘lost in the middle’ research (Liu et al., 2023).
entries.source_title: Context Rot: How Increasing Input Tokens Impacts LLM Performance — Chroma

entries.plain_def: The telltale chatbot writing voice — smooth, generic, over-polite, full of ‘delve,’ ‘tapestry,’ and tidy three-point lists. Shorthand for ‘this reads like an LLM wrote it.’
entries.milestone_note: Informal coinage after ChatGPT’s public boom (late 2022–2023). No single inventor; widely used in editing/ crit circles. Also called AI voice or GPT-isms.

entries.plain_def: An app whose ‘brains’ are mostly someone else’s model API (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.), with your UI, prompts, and workflow on top. ‘Thin wrapper’ is often a dig: little moat beyond a prompt.
entries.milestone_note: Investor/builder slang ~2023– onward as API-first AI apps proliferated. Neutral architectural label; pejorative when the product is only a thin prompt layer.
entries.source_title: What is an AI wrapper? — CRV

entries.plain_def: When a model confidently makes stuff up — fake facts, fake citations, fake details — presented as if true. Not ‘seeing things’; it’s fluent guessing gone wrong.
entries.milestone_note: Term in wide AI use since early ChatGPT era (~2022–23). OpenAI’s Sept 2025 paper ‘Why language models hallucinate’ argues training/evals reward guessing over saying ‘I don’t know.’

entries.plain_def: Reusable playbooks for AI agents — usually a folder with a SKILL.md (plus optional scripts) that teaches the agent how to do a specific job when the task matches.
entries.milestone_note: Anthropic introduced Agent Skills Oct 16, 2025; published as an open standard (agentskills.io) Dec 18, 2025. Adopted by Cursor, Claude Code, and others.
entries.source_title: Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills — Anthropic
